newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thai Copper inks pact with Chile's Codelco.
newsitem.headline: Thai Copper inks pact with Chile's Codelco.

text.p: Thai Copper Industries and Chilean mining giant Codelco on Wednesday signed a technology agreement for the Thai company's copper smelter.

The US$600 million smelter, Thailand's first, will be operational in 1998 and will have a capacity of 185,000 tonnes a year, Thai Copper chairman and chief executive officer Prayudh Mahagitsiri told reporters after signing the deal in Singapore.
"Most of the production capacity is for domestic (consumption)," he said of the smelter, which is located in eastern Rayong province.

Prayudh said Thai demand for refined copper, which now stands between 160,000-190,000 tonnes a year, will easily outstrip the smelter's capacity because demand for the metal is growing around 15 percent a year.
Fernando Riveri, general manager of Codelco's El Teniente mine, signed the agreement for his company.
He said the three-year pact, which is worth $50 million for Codelco, requires the Chilean firm to help Thai Copper to provide technical assistance and training in the startup of the smelter.
"Our responsibility is for the converter in the smelter," he said, adding about 50 Chilean technicians will fly to Thailand to help train local personnel.
Prayudh said copper for the new smelter will probably be sourced from Chile, Indonesia, Canada and Australia.
